solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pass, possibly, due to expire soon

parts.note: read the solution as instructions: a word for old-fashioned, cut short by one letter, gives this clue word; 'possibly' flags the roundabout route

explanation.surface: A permit or ticket that is about to run out.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: DATED is PASSÉ, and SHORT says to drop its last letter, leaving PASS. Bloggers found it a stretch; 'Pass' wants to be a ticket, but it is the result of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods or bonds labelled with a near expiry are described this way, meaning their useful life is about to end.

clue.text: This brown dog barking could become so raged

indicators.note: barking is slang for mad, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A noisy brown dog getting very angry.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer and DOG together, mixed up, could become SO RAGED.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch the outside of meat in a hot pan is to brown it.

clue.text: Writing found on arms after overturning a new seat

indicators.note: after places the a-new pair behind the turned words
overturning means the writing reads backwards

parts.note: a coat of arms usually bears a motto

explanation.surface: Inscription on a chair's arms found when it's turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' is heraldry, not chair arms or weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded upholstered bench or footstool, often with storage, is a seat.

clue.text: Woman of strange power under acrobat's control

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts the woman after the acrobat's

parts.note: an acrobat is a tumbler, with the possessive S
a witch is a woman with magical powers

explanation.surface: A sorceress held in the grip of a circus performer.
explanation.definitionFit: This toggle device for lights flips over with a click, so it is an electrical control.

clue.text: Gold and other metal found beneath South American city

indicators.note: in a down clue, found beneath places the metal below south

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
tin is another metal

explanation.surface: Precious metals discovered below a city in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Texas is a US city, so it is American.

clue.text: Risk death — drive up the wall

parts.note: death is one's end
to drive someone up the wall is to infuriate them

explanation.surface: Danger of death makes one go crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something at risk is to imperil it, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Quarterly, aeroplane in Essex takes off

indicators.note: something quarterly comes every fourth time, so every fourth letter is taken, starting from the first

explanation.surface: A plane flying around a county east of London that departs four times a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarterly' picks the 1st, 5th, 9th and 13th letters of 'aeroplane in Essex'. Essex is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic them, which is exactly what copying someone like a monkey means.

clue.text: With support around, I open up

indicators.note: around means the support goes about the I word

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar of a bridge
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone opening up with support around them.
explanation.definitionFit: To be first to explore or develop new territory is to open it up.

clue.text: Bowled over by big hitter, son admitted to beginning fight

indicators.note: admitted to means the son goes inside the beginning word

parts.note: the beginning is the start
a ruck is a scuffle or fight

explanation.surface: A cricket batsman knocked over by a powerful hitter, his son at the start of a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Overawed in the presence of a celebrity, i.e. a big name, so dazzled.

clue.text: Greek goddess to fail endlessly going after cunning European

indicators.note: this places the shortened failure word after the cunning and European pieces

parts.note: cunning or craft is art, as in artful

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to fail to hit is to miss

explanation.surface: A deity who keeps falling short, following a crafty continental.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the Olympian huntress and moon deity, twin of Apollo in Greek myth.

clue.text: Not unknown in Olympiad to struggle for qualification

indicators.note: to struggle suggests the remaining letters are thrown about into a new order
'Not unknown in' says the unknown letter is removed from the word that follows

parts.note: Y is one of the algebraic unknowns, x, y and z

explanation.surface: An athlete who struggles at the Games to qualify.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not unknown in Olympiad' takes Y out, leaving OLMPIAD, which 'to struggle' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A certificate awarded on completing a course is an academic qualification.

clue.text: Nerd is troubled with 18 questions about procedure

indicators.note: troubled indicates the letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: the solution to 18 down, the top of a building

explanation.surface: A geek on a building's top, worried about formal matters.
explanation.definitionFit: In a meeting, these are queries raised about whether the rules of debate are being followed.

clue.text: Girl trapping big cat in den close to snare she's loaded

indicators.note: trapping means the girl word encloses everything that follows

parts.note: a girl is a miss

indicators.note: in places the cat inside the den

parts.note: an animal's den is its lair
the lion is the big cat

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of snare

explanation.surface: A young woman catches a lion in its lair and becomes rich.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who is loaded has a great fortune, a female with a seven-figure wealth.

clue.text: Image beneath skull generally frustrated doctor

parts.note: someone frustrated is cross, annoyed
Bones (from sawbones) is a nickname for a doctor, as in Star Trek

explanation.surface: An irritated medic.
explanation.definitionFit: The pirate flag shows two bones crossed below a skull, the usual picture with it.

clue.text: King getting amorous outside was exhausted

indicators.note: outside means the amorous word wraps around the king

parts.note: amorous, feeling lusty, is randy
R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex)

explanation.surface: A monarch in an amorous mood who ends up worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: A supply that has run out has been used up, like a well with no water left.

clue.text: Lounge layout disheartened artisan

parts.note: to lounge is to rest

indicators.note: disheartened means the central letter is removed

parts.note: a layout or arrangement is an order

explanation.surface: A craftsman left depressed by the design of a sitting room.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsperson who repairs old furniture or paintings is a skilled artisan.

clue.text: Fashionista not using an agent

definitions.meaning: a trendy individual, one who is 'in'
personally, oneself rather than through a representative

explanation.surface: A fashion devotee who does her own deals.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of trends is an in person, and dealing personally means appearing yourself.

clue.text: Confess about team cheating

indicators.note: about means the confession word goes around the team

parts.note: in slang, to sing is to confess to the police
a team, especially of rowers, is a crew

explanation.surface: Admitting that a sports team has been cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for swindling or defrauding someone, so it means cheating.

clue.text: Mounted low-grade brackets frequently for upper side of structure

indicators.note: brackets means the reversed word encloses the next piece
in a down clue, mounted means the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: low-grade means poor
oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: Cheap shelf supports often put up on a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The top outside surface of a building is its upper side.

clue.text: Drink might become cold if rejected

indicators.note: rejected means the phrase is turned back to front

parts.note: might, as in may be able to, is can
to become, as in go cold, is go
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A drink that turns cold if sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might become cold' reads as CAN GO C; 'if rejected' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This French brandy is a spirit, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Groupie upset, party is least worthwhile

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a groupie is a devoted fan
a fest is a festival or party

explanation.surface: A distressed rock follower decides a party is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: NAFF is British slang for tacky or worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of a British slang word for rubbish, so most worthless.

clue.text: Hot skewer with starter removed under force

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts the shortened skewer below the force

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force

indicators.note: starter removed means the first letter goes

parts.note: to skewer is to pierce

explanation.surface: A hot kebab skewer loses its first piece under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense and ferocious, as fierce heat or a heated temper, so hot in that sense.

clue.text: Curses to that swimming pool with couple of females bare

parts.note: 'Blow!' is a mild curse
the definite article that singles out a thing
a lido is a public open-air swimming pool
F is the abbreviation for female, so two of them

explanation.surface: Swearing at an outdoor pool where two women are undressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curses to that swimming pool' reads as 'Blow the lido!', a mild British oath; a lido is a public open-air pool.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose a scandal is to lay it bare, revealing what was hidden.

clue.text: Scratching so, drunk gets treated

indicators.note: scratching means crossing out or deleting

parts.note: soused is slang for drunk
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk scratching himself gets medical treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: To have exploited someone is to have treated them badly, so used here means handled.

clue.text: Scores owned by revolutionary? On the contrary

parts.note: on the contrary negates the statement, adding not
Che Guevara is the revolutionary, so his things are Che's

explanation.surface: A question whether some music belongs to a radical, answered with a denial.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as 'scores are Che's? No, NOT CHE'S'; Che Guevara is the crossword's usual revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks cut to keep a tally are scores, as in nicks on a stick.

clue.text: Relief to get back into gear

definitions.meaning: relief meaning remedy or compensation for a wrong
to put clothes on again, gear being clothing

explanation.surface: Relief at being able to change back into your kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Redress is compensation for a wrong, and re-dress means to clothe oneself again.

clue.text: Missing nothing, adds cleaning material to drains

indicators.note: missing means the nothing letter is taken out

parts.note: to put soap on something is to soap it
O is the round zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone cleaning the drains with soap, leaving nothing out.
explanation.definitionFit: To sap strength is to drain it away gradually, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: United, twice ignoring wingers in side, target nine to back

indicators.note: to back means the hidden letters are read backwards
the letters are found inside the words, with the end letters stripped away twice

explanation.surface: A football team united, leaving out wide players and aiming for a ninth win.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'side target nine' backwards gives ENINTEGRATEDIS; 'twice ignoring wingers' strips the outer pair twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Things integrated have been combined into one whole, so they are unified.
